Analyst report · Q1 FY2026/27 · Confidence medium

The Rank Group Plc

A clean but unspectacular Q1: group LFL NGR +5% to £216.1m (~$286.5m), with Grosvenor gaming machines (+14%) doing the heavy lifting and UK digital (+6%) holding up through its first full quarter under 40% Remote Gaming Duty. FY27 operating-profit guidance is reiterated but explicitly conditional on no change to Machine Games Duty — the Autumn Budget, not the trading, sets the equity's value from here, and the undisclosed in-quarter deceleration (first six weeks +8%, full quarter +5%) is the number management chose not to highlight.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Entain plc

An "as guided" quarter with the UK doing all the heavy lifting: Q3 group NGR +2% cc, online +3% (+5% ex-Brazil) and UK&I online +14% on +15% volumes, against a ~4pp drag from customer-friendly football and a -36% Brazil print that precedes a full Q4 wipe-out. FY26 guidance — online NGR +4-6% cc and underlying EBITDA at the lower end of £910-960m (~$1.20-1.27bn) — was reiterated three weeks after being cut to the floor, so the ~3% share-price fall reflects quality-of-growth questions (sports NGR -3%, International online -3%, ex-Brazil International only +1%, a "softer Q4" nod from the CFO) rather than any new estimate change. BetMGM's $86m adjusted EBITDA (+112%) and $68m of cash to parents is the genuine positive surprise.

Analyst report · Q1 FY2027 · Confidence medium

The Rank Group plc

A clean but revenue-only Q1: LFL NGR +5% to £216.1m (~$287m), digital +6% and Grosvenor +6% (machines +14%) absorbing the first full quarter of 40% Remote Gaming Duty, with FY27 guidance reiterated as "in line with market expectations" — explicitly conditional on no Budget change to Machine Games Duty. The print neither re-rates nor de-rates the equity; the stock remains a binary on the Autumn Budget, where Shore Capital sizes a hypothetical MGD doubling at £35m (~$47m) gross against FY26 underlying operating profit of £78.6m (~$105m). Beneath the headline, growth decelerated through the quarter (first six weeks +8%, full quarter +5%) and Mecca visits fell again.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Okada Manila

A flat-revenue, hold-flattered quarter. Q3-26 revenue of ₱7,841m (~$124.7m) was unchanged YoY and GGR rose just 0.9% to ₱7.04bn (~$111.9m) only because live mass-table hold jumped 380bps to 32.2%; VIP rolling volume fell another 28% and adjusted segment EBITDA dropped 13% to ₱962m (~$15.3m), a 12.3% margin (-180bps). The sequential rebound from a dire Q2 (₱333m) keeps parent UEC's "2H26 return to IR operating profit" target technically alive, but hold-adjusted GGR was still down ~1% and the cost base grew 2% on flat revenue — this is stabilisation, not recovery.

Analyst report · FY26 · Confidence medium

Betfred

Betfred's last set of accounts before the UK duty shock shows a group that is growing online (+20% on a 52-week pro-rata basis, now 45% of turnover) but whose profitability has already compressed sharply: EBITDA of £140.6m is ~28% below the pro-rata run-rate of the prior 78-week period and the margin is down ~600bps to 14.1%, before a single pound of the 40% RGD hits. With retail shrinking ~9% pro-rata, 132 further shop closures under way, a 76% dividend payout and management now withholding geographic disclosure, this is a business entering the FY27 tax regime with far less cushion than the £996m turnover headline suggests.

Analyst report · FY26 · Confidence medium

Singapore Pools

A third straight record year — turnover +6.2% to S$13.48bn with growth re-accelerating from +4% and no mega sporting event in the period — but the incremental dollar went almost entirely to prizes, opex and the Exchequer: betting duties & taxes rose 9% to S$2.49bn while the Tote Board contribution (the only "earnings" line the entity reports) was flat at S$583m (+1.4%). For sector investors the read-through is a still-growing Singapore gambling wallet and a monopoly lottery/tote model where the state captures ~88% of implied gross win before costs; this is a fiscal instrument first and an operating business second, and it discloses accordingly.

Analyst report · H1 FY2027 · Confidence medium

PointsBet Holdings

PointsBet pre-announced a sharp H1 FY27 miss: revenue ~A$113m (-16% YoY vs A$135m) and a normalised EBITDA loss of A$6–8m, entirely attributable to Australia, where self-imposed VIP compliance tightening has cut highest-value-cohort turnover/revenue by double digits all half and a deliberate mass-market push ran into punter-friendly AFL results and promo/product-fee dilution from the Pull 'Em product. The Canada/iGaming growth leg (FY26 revenue +13%) is intact but, at ~18% of group, is too small to carry a structurally de-rated Australian book; with cash of roughly A$23m and a 66%-owned register, the quarter re-opens the question of how long MIXI tolerates a listed, loss-making minority structure.

Analyst report · Q2 2026 · Confidence high

Flutter Entertainment plc

A headline beat with a hollow core: revenue +3% and adj. EBITDA $508m landed above consensus, but the fourth consecutive guidance cut (FY26 adj. EBITDA to $2.655bn, -7% YoY) is entirely a US decision to spend ~$270m more on generosity in H2, taken on the day the CEO announced his exit. International is doing its job (+4% organic, SEA +18%) while absorbing the UK duty step-up; the US is being re-based for a second time in nine months, leverage is 4.3x and the proof point is now Q4 (US EBITDA ~$500m vs ~$700m previously).

Analyst report · Q2 2026 · Confidence high

Evolution AB

An in-line, marginally light quarter that confirms the new shape of Evolution: a ~66%-margin cash machine whose growth now comes from the Americas and RNG, while Europe stabilises and Asia (37% of end-player revenue) stays hostage to content piracy. Net revenue fell 1.2% to EUR 517.8m (+2.4% constant currency) and EBITDA fell 1.2% to EUR 341.0m at a flat 65.9% margin; EPS still rose 4.7% because the EUR 2bn buyback and a financial-items swing did the work. Until Asia and Europe both grow, the equity case is capital return plus product optionality rather than compounding growth.
